documents.title: Proposed Faculty Syllabus Statement Options Concerning Artificial Intelligence
documents.summary: A Faculty Senate committee proposal that suggests every syllabus carry an AI statement. It gives a shared misconduct statement and three optional course statements (embrace, limited, prohibit) that instructors pick from or replace.
documents.stance_why: The document sets no single rule. It says 'Suggested options are provided below' and gives a 'choice of more specific policy options' (embrace, limited, prohibit), so the decision goes to instructors and the stance is delegates with tiers.

units.why: The committee asks all faculty to put an AI statement in their syllabi: 'It is suggested that all faculty include in their syllabi some statement'. It is a recommendation, so modality is should; P09 fits because it concerns stating AI expectations in the syllabus.
units.anchor: all faculty include in their syllabi some statement concerning the use of AI
units.frag_end: use of AI in their classes

units.why: Faculty may write their own statement instead of the options: 'faculty are also welcome to write their own statements'. This leaves wording to each instructor, so P04 rather than P09.
units.anchor: faculty are also welcome to write their own statements

units.why: The document offers a menu of three course-level options (embrace, limited, prohibit) for instructors to pick from: 'a choice of more specific policy options'. That is a set of named tiers, so P05; P04 also fits but the tiers are the distinctive content.
units.anchor: followed by a choice of more specific policy options
units.frag_start: It is followed by a choice
units.policy: Faculty may choose among three course policy options: embrace AI, allow limited use of AI, or prohibit AI.
units.fit_note: Also shows the instructor chooses the tier (P04).

units.why: The general statement says misuse 'may be academic misconduct and/or a violation of discipline-specific professional ethics'. It classifies inappropriate or unauthorized AI content as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: inappropriate or unauthorized use of AI-generated content may be academic misconduct

units.why: The statement says misuse 'will be handled according to TCU's Academic Conduct Policy or other relevant policies'. This routes AI misuse to the existing conduct process, so P36 (nearest type); it extends the rule to other assignment-help tools.
units.anchor: will be handled according to TCU’s Academic Conduct Policy or other relevant policies
units.fit_note: Also covers 'other assignment-help tools', not only AI.

units.why: The statement lists penalties: 'sanctions, including failing the course, program dismissal, suspension, or expulsion'. Concrete penalties are stated in advance, so P37.
units.anchor: may result in sanctions, including failing the course, program dismissal, suspension, or expulsion

units.why: Option A says 'Artificial intelligence may be used for any assignment with appropriate citation'. It is a permissive default for instructors who embrace AI, so P02; the citation condition is coded separately.
units.anchor: Artificial intelligence may be used for any assignment with appropriate citation

units.why: Option A points to citation examples: 'Examples of such citations can be found online, for example at APA.' Students must cite AI use and the text points to APA format, so P24 (disclosure); it does not name tool, prompt or date, so P25 does not fit.
units.anchor: Examples of such citations can be found online, for example at APA
units.fit_note: Points to APA citation examples without specifying tool, prompt or date.

units.why: Option A says 'You are responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI.' Students must verify AI output, so P31.
units.anchor: You are responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI

units.why: Option A says 'The use of AI should not replace your critical thinking, judgment, and topic expertise.' The student stays the thinker, so P32.
units.anchor: The use of AI should not replace your critical thinking, judgment, and topic expertise

units.why: Option B allows AI only for some assignment types: 'may be used for [assignment types A, B & C] with appropriate citation, but not for [assignment types D, E & F]'. This is a per-assignment limited-use rule, so P04; the permission is conditional on citation.
units.anchor: may be used for [assignment types A, B & C] with appropriate citation
units.policy: AI may be used for the assignment types the instructor lists, with appropriate citation, but not for the other listed assignment types.
units.fit_note: Template for a limited-use policy; P05 also fits as the middle tier.

units.why: Option B says 'If you are in doubt as to whether you are using AI appropriately in this course, it is your responsibility to discuss your situation with the instructor.' Students unsure must ask, so P10.
units.anchor: in doubt as to whether you are using AI appropriately in this course
units.frag_start: If you are in doubt as

units.why: Option B has its own citation requirement ('with appropriate citation' for the permitted assignment types). It is a separate template from option A, so it is coded again as disclosure, P24.
units.anchor: with appropriate citation, but not for [assignment types D, E & F]
units.policy: Students must cite AI used for the permitted assignment types.

units.why: Option B repeats 'You are responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI.' in its own template, so it is coded for option B; verification, P31.
units.anchor: responsible for fact-checking statements composed by AI

units.why: Option C says AI 'MAY NOT be used for course assignments except as explicitly authorized by the instructor'. A ban unless authorized is P01 as the default rule for instructors who prohibit; it covers unapproved assignment-help tools too.
units.anchor: MAY NOT be used for course assignments except as explicitly authorized by the instructor

units.why: Option C prohibits 'Submitting all or any part of an assignment statement to an AI'. Pasting the assignment into AI is the P20 type.
units.anchor: Submitting all or any part of an assignment statement to an AI or unapproved

units.why: Option C prohibits 'Incorporating any part of an AI-generated response in an assignment', i.e. AI-produced work submitted, so P19.
units.anchor: Incorporating any part of an AI-generated response in an assignment
units.fit_note: Covers any AI-generated response, not only code.

units.why: Option C prohibits 'Using AI to brainstorm, formulate arguments, or template ideas'. This forbids the brainstorming use that P15 permits, and nothing is submitted as generated, so P19 does not fit; no prohibited type covers it, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Using AI to brainstorm, formulate arguments, or template ideas for assignments
units.uncovered_note: Bans using AI for brainstorming, forming arguments or templating ideas, a prohibition on idea generation rather than on submitted output.

units.why: Option C prohibits 'Using AI to summarize or contextualize source materials'. Banning AI for summarizing reading is the reverse of P14 and fits no prohibited type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Using AI to summarize or contextualize source materials
units.uncovered_note: Bans using AI to summarize or contextualize source materials.

units.why: Option C prohibits 'Submitting your own work for this class to an AI ... for iteration or improvement', i.e. feeding one's own work to AI to improve it, so P20 (P21 also touches it, but P20 names submitting work to the tool).
units.anchor: Submitting your own work for this class to an AI
units.fit_note: Purpose named is iteration or improvement of the student's own work (also P21).

units.why: Option C says 'If you are in doubt as to what constitutes AI, or whether an assignment-help tool is suitable ... it is your responsibility to discuss your situation with the instructor.' Students must ask when unsure, so P10.
units.anchor: If you are in doubt as to what constitutes AI

documents.unit: Mary Couts Burnett Library (quoting the Student Handbook)
documents.title: TCU AI Policy for Students (Academic Misconduct 10. Unauthorized Use of AI), quoted by the library
documents.summary: A library FAQ that quotes one sentence of the student conduct policy. Generative AI use without documented instructor or syllabus approval counts as misrepresenting someone else's work.
documents.stance_why: The quoted policy says generative AI used 'without documented approval from the course instructor or in the syllabus' is misconduct, so AI is banned unless approved. That is restrict.

units.why: The library quotes the Student Handbook: using generative AI 'without documented approval from the course instructor or in the syllabus' is misconduct. It sets a fallback of no AI unless approved, so P06.
units.anchor: Using generative AI without documented approval from the course instructor or in the syllabus
units.fit_note: Approval can be documented by instructor or syllabus.

units.why: The same sentence says such use 'will be considered equivalent to representing someone else's work as one's own'. This classifies unapproved AI use as misconduct, so P36.
units.anchor: will be considered equivalent to representing someone else’s work as one’s own

notes: Second document is a thin secondary quote; the full TCU AI policy was not collected. The first is a committee proposal, adoption unconfirmed.
